newsitem.title: USA: Lazare Kaplan Q4 hurt by shipment delays.
newsitem.headline: Lazare Kaplan Q4 hurt by shipment delays.

text.p: Lazare Kaplan International Inc said on Thursday that its fourth quarter earnings per share should be about $0.43 to $0.45 reflecting delays in receiving Russian diamonds, compared with $0.28 a share reported for the year ago fourth quarter.

Earnings from continuing operations for the fourth quarter ended May 31, 1997 are estimated to be between $0.50 and $0.52 a share, including a gain of $0.38 a share from accounting rules relating to a reserve equal to the deferred tax asset.

Lazare Kaplan said it has not received shipment of any polished diamonds from Russia, which has hurt fourth quarter earnings by $0.23 to $0.28 a share, but it expects to recapture lost sales once the diamonds are exported.

Fourth quarter results will also be hurt by its decision to discontinue efforts to partake in the privatization of the Akwatia and Birim deposits owned and operated by Ghana Consolidated Diamonds Ltd.
The discontinued operation will reduce earnings by $0.07 a share, the company said.
Lazare Kaplan expects fiscal year earnings per share of $1.52 to $1.54, compared with $1.12 a share on sales of $266.3 million in the year ended May 31, 1996.
The company expects to issue its report of earnings for the fiscal year ended May 31, 1997 on July 9.

Lazare Kaplan's chairman, Maurice Tempelsman and company president Leon Tempelsman met with Russian officials about that nation's diamond trade policy and that new government procedures on exporting the diamonds are imminent, the company said.

Shortages of quality rough diamonds have developed, partially attributable to the stoppage of Russian rough shipments, and have caused price rises in the cost of raw materials that are not yet reflected in the price of the polished diamonds, Lazare Kaplan said.

In the short term this has resulted in margin pressure, but longer term benefits will eventually be derived from the Company's strong marketing, rough sourcing and inventory positions, the company said.
